title: Ruy Lopez: the ideas
line: The bishop presses on the knight that guards Black's center pawn.

steps.text: Push the pawn in front of your king two squares. It takes space in the center and frees your queen and a bishop.

also.d2d4: Pushing the queen's pawn is also sound and leads to other openings. This lesson pushes the king's pawn.

steps.text: Bring the knight out to attack Black's pawn on e5.

also.b1c3: That is the Vienna Game, also sound. This lesson brings this knight out.
also.f1c4: That is the Bishop's Opening, also sound. This lesson brings the knight out first.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out to attack the knight that guards the pawn.

also.f1c4: That is the Italian Game, also sound. This lesson goes to b5.
also.d2d4: That is the Scotch Game, also sound. This lesson brings the bishop out.
also.b1c3: That leads to the Four Knights Game, also sound. This lesson brings the bishop out.

steps.after: This is the Ruy Lopez. Black asks the bishop what it will do.

steps.text: Step the bishop back. It keeps its eye on the knight.

also.b5c6: Taking the knight is the Exchange Variation, a lesson of its own. This lesson keeps the bishop.

steps.after: The knight attacks your pawn on e4.

steps.text: Castle and let the pawn on e4 hang. If the knight takes it, you get it back, as the Open Ruy Lopez lesson shows.
steps.after: Black gets ready to castle. The pressure on the knight lasts a long time.

steps.text: Why the pressure matters: in this line Black guarded the pawn with a pawn and castled too soon, a slip club players often make.
Take the knight that guards the pawn on e5. A bishop takes back.
Take the pawn on e5. A pawn takes back, and the file between the two queens opens.
Trade queens first. If you take the pawn at once, Black trades queens itself and gets a pawn back.
steps.hint: Your queen and Black's queen face each other on the same file.

steps.text: Take the pawn on e5 with your knight. Nothing guards it now.
steps.after: A pawn up. Take away the knight that guards the pawn and the pawn falls.

summary: The bishop presses on the knight that guards the center pawn. If that knight goes, the pawn often goes with it.
